title: Electronic Components & Devices
description: Input devices, output devices, process components, passive components, power supplies, and wiring types for OCR R047.
content_html:
Input Components and Devices

Input devices convert a physical quantity or user action into an electrical signal. The OCR specification covers several switch types: the Single Pole Single Throw (SPST) switch simply opens or closes one circuit; a push-to-make switch connects the circuit only while pressed; a push-to-break switch disconnects the circuit while pressed. A tilt switch contains a small ball bearing that completes or breaks the circuit when tilted — used in safety cut-offs. A reed switch is a magnetically operated switch: two metal contacts inside a glass capsule close when a magnet is brought close — common in door and window alarms. A Quantum Tunnelling Composite (QTC) switch uses a material whose resistance changes when compressed, enabling pressure-sensitive switching without moving parts.

Sensor input devices include: a Light Dependent Resistor (LDR), whose resistance falls as light increases — used in automatic lighting circuits; a photodiode, which conducts in proportion to incident light — faster and more precise than an LDR; an NTC thermistor (Negative Temperature Coefficient), whose resistance falls as temperature rises — used in temperature measurement and control; a pressure sensor, which converts mechanical force into an electrical signal; an infrared sensor, which detects infrared radiation — used in motion detectors and remote controls; and smart (WiFi-enabled) sensors, which connect to a network to transmit data remotely. Touch screens are also listed as input devices — they detect the position of a finger or stylus on a display surface.

Process Components and Devices

Process components manipulate signals between input and output. Amplifiers increase signal voltage or current. Counters count pulses or events. Timers generate a timed output after a set delay (e.g. the 555 timer IC). Latches store a binary state — once triggered, they hold their output until reset. Pulse generators produce repetitive clock signals. Analogue to digital converters (ADCs) sample an analogue input and convert it to a binary number — essential for connecting sensors to microcontrollers. Logic functions (AND, OR, NOT, NAND) are digital process components whose outputs depend on combinations of binary inputs. You must know their truth tables and be able to apply them singly and in two-level combinations.

Key Fact

Input switches: SPST, push-to-make, push-to-break, tilt, reed, QTC. Input sensors: LDR, photodiode, NTC thermistor, pressure sensor, infrared sensor, smart sensor. Output devices: lamps, LEDs, LED displays, LCDs, buzzers, piezo sounders, motors. Drivers/interface: NPN transistor, Darlington driver, relay. Passive: resistors (fixed, variable), diodes, capacitors (polarised, non-polarised).

Output Components and Devices

Lamps produce light from current; they require relatively high current and are less efficient than LEDs. Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) are semiconductor devices that emit light when forward biased — low current, long life, available in many colours. LED displays (7-segment and dot-matrix) are arrays of LEDs configured to display numbers, letters, and symbols. Liquid Crystal Displays (LCDs) use liquid crystal cells to modulate light — very low power, used in clocks, meters, and screens. Buzzers use an electromagnetic mechanism to produce sound when current flows; piezo sounders use a piezoelectric disc that vibrates when an alternating voltage is applied — smaller and more power-efficient than buzzers. Motors convert electrical energy into rotational mechanical energy.

Drivers, Passive Components, Power Supplies and Wiring

Higher-power output devices need driver components because microcontrollers supply only a few milliamps. An NPN transistor amplifies current — a small base current switches a much larger collector-emitter current. A Darlington driver pairs two NPN transistors for very high current gain. A relay closes a separate high-power switching contact using a small electromagnet current, electrically isolating the control circuit from the load. Passive components need no supply: fixed resistors set resistance; variable resistors adjust it; diodes pass current in one direction only; capacitors store charge — polarised (electrolytic) types must be connected the right way round, non-polarised types can go either way. Power supply options: batteries (portable DC); photovoltaic cells (renewable, light-dependent output); supercapacitors (rapid charge/discharge, limited energy storage); mains adaptors (stable DC from AC mains). Wiring: single-strand (solid core) holds shape — ideal for breadboard; multi-strand (flexible) bends without breaking — used where connections must flex.

Key Fact

NPN transistors and Darlington drivers switch high-current loads using a small control current. Relays provide electrical isolation between the control circuit and the load — essential when switching mains-voltage devices from a low-voltage microcontroller. Polarised capacitors must be connected with the correct polarity or they can be damaged.

NTC stands for Negative Temperature Coefficient. As temperature rises, more electrons gain enough energy to become charge carriers, so more current flows for the same voltage — meaning resistance is lower (R = V ÷ I). This resistance change is used in a voltage divider circuit to produce a varying voltage that a microcontroller reads and compares with a threshold to trigger a heating or cooling output.

Battery: portable but must be replaced or recharged — good for handheld devices, poor for long-term field sensors. Photovoltaic cell: renewable and maintenance-free in daylight, but output varies with light and a buffer store is needed for night use. Supercapacitor: charges and discharges very rapidly, long cycle life, but stores far less total energy than a battery — suited to brief backup or energy harvesting. Mains adaptor: reliable, constant output, but needs a socket — ideal for fixed, indoor devices only.
exam_tip_html: When an OCR question asks you to 'identify a suitable input device' or 'choose an appropriate output component', always justify your choice in terms of the physical quantity being sensed or the form of energy being converted — do not just name the component. For example: 'an LDR is suitable because its resistance changes with light intensity, which can be used to vary the voltage in a circuit to detect day and night.' Component symbol questions require you to recognise the symbol, not just name the component — practise sketching the symbols for LED, LDR, NPN transistor, relay, and NTC thermistor.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • Input devices convert physical quantities into electrical signals: switches respond to user action; sensors (LDR, NTC thermistor, photodiode, infrared, pressure, smart) respond to environmental quantities.
  • Output devices convert electrical signals: LEDs and lamps produce light; buzzers and piezo sounders produce sound; motors produce rotational movement; LCDs and LED displays produce visual information.
  • Driver components (NPN transistors, Darlington drivers, relays) allow a low-current control signal to switch a high-current load; relays also provide electrical isolation between the control circuit and the switched circuit.

glossary_terms.definition: A switch with a single input and a single output contact that either makes or breaks the circuit — the most basic on/off switch type.
A resistor whose resistance decreases as light intensity increases; used to detect ambient light levels.
A pair of NPN transistors wired so that the output of the first drives the base of the second, giving a very high combined current gain, used to drive high-power loads such as motors.
An electrically operated switch in which a small control current through an electromagnet closes a separate set of contacts to switch a higher-power circuit.

practice_questions.text:
Which of the following sensors is most suitable for detecting temperature changes in a room thermostat?
A) Light Dependent Resistor (LDR)
B) Reed switch
C) NTC thermistor
D) Photodiode
State two differences between a buzzer and a piezo sounder.
practice_questions.marks: One mark each for any two from: a buzzer uses an electromagnetic mechanism / a piezo sounder uses a piezoelectric disc; a piezo sounder is smaller and more power-efficient than a buzzer; a buzzer requires DC / a piezo sounder responds to an alternating voltage; buzzers are generally lower frequency than piezo sounders. [2 marks]

practice_questions.text: Explain why a transistor or relay is needed between a microcontroller and a motor in a circuit.
practice_questions.marks: 1 mark: a microcontroller output can only supply a small current (typically a few milliamps). 1 mark: a motor requires a much higher current to operate. 1 mark: a transistor or relay acts as a switch/amplifier — the small microcontroller current controls the base of the transistor (or the relay coil), which switches the larger motor current through the collector-emitter path (or relay contacts). Accept relay also provides electrical isolation. [3 marks]

practice_questions.text: Describe the purpose of a relay and give one advantage it has over using an NPN transistor to switch a high-power load.
practice_questions.marks:
Purpose (2 marks): a relay uses a small electromagnet — activated by a low control current — to mechanically close a separate set of contacts, switching a higher-power circuit on or off (2 marks for full description; 1 mark for partial).
Advantage (2 marks): a relay provides electrical isolation — the control circuit (e.g. microcontroller at 3.3 V) and the switched circuit (e.g. 230 V mains load) are completely separated, reducing the risk of high voltages damaging the control electronics. An NPN transistor does not provide this isolation (2 marks for specific, applied advantage; 1 mark for vague). [4 marks total]

practice_questions.text:
A student is designing a garden security light that switches on automatically at night and off during the day. The light uses a 12 V, 5 W LED floodlight.

Discuss the choice of input sensor and driver component for this system.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (5–6 marks): a balanced discussion covering at least two factors with development. Input sensor: an LDR is appropriate because its resistance increases in the dark and decreases in bright light — in a voltage divider circuit, this produces a voltage change that can be compared with a threshold to detect night/day (developed, applied to scenario). Driver component: the LED floodlight draws P ÷ V = 5 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.42 A of current — far more than a microcontroller or comparator can supply directly — so an NPN transistor or relay is needed (calculation shown, component justified). Relay advantage: if the circuit uses a mains-powered floodlight instead of 12 V, a relay is essential for electrical isolation (counter-argument/extension considered). Limitation: an LDR responds slowly compared to a photodiode, which could cause flicker at dawn/dusk — a timer or Schmitt trigger could be added to prevent rapid switching (further development).
Secure (3–4 marks): input sensor and driver both identified and briefly justified, some reference to the scenario.
Developing (2 marks): one component identified with limited justification.
Emerging (1 mark): a single relevant point with no development. [6 marks]

practice_questions.text:
A smart home system uses a range of sensors (temperature, light, motion) connected to a central microcontroller. The system controls heating, lighting, and a security alarm.

Evaluate the suitability of different power supply types for the sensors in this system, considering both performance and sustainability.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (7–8 marks): a balanced evaluation covering at least three power supply types with specific application to smart home sensors, supported by reasoning and a clear judgement. Battery: portable and self-contained — sensors can be placed anywhere, but batteries require periodic replacement, which has cost and environmental implications; rechargeable batteries reduce waste but need maintenance (developed, applied). Photovoltaic cells: sustainable and maintenance-free for outdoor sensors (e.g. motion sensor near a window or garden) — output varies with light so a supercapacitor or rechargeable battery is needed as a buffer; not suitable for sensors in dark locations indoors (developed, limitation identified). Supercapacitor: charges and discharges very rapidly — suitable for brief energy harvesting or backup between periods of mains power, but stores much less energy than a battery so cannot power a sensor long-term during a mains outage (developed, limitation identified). Mains adaptor: most reliable and consistent — suitable for fixed, indoor sensors such as a thermostat or security camera, but requires wiring and proximity to a socket, limiting placement flexibility (developed). Judgement: for a smart home system, a combination of supply types is most suitable — mains adaptors for fixed, high-power sensors; photovoltaic + supercapacitor for outdoor sensors; batteries for portable or hard-to-wire locations — no single supply type meets all requirements.
Secure (5–6 marks): three supply types covered with application and an attempt at a judgement.
Developing (3–4 marks): two supply types covered with limited application.
Emerging (1–2 marks): basic points, no evaluation. [8 marks]

knowledge_checks.q: Which of the following input sensors changes resistance in response to changes in temperature?
Which driver component provides electrical isolation between the control circuit and the high-power load?
A _____ switch closes its contacts when a magnet is brought close to it.
In an NTC thermistor, as temperature increases, resistance _____.
Match each component to its primary function.
right: Switches a high-power circuit using a small control current with electrical isolation
Varies resistance in response to changes in light intensity

flashcard_questions.q: What does LDR stand for and how does it behave?
flashcard_questions.a: LDR stands for Light Dependent Resistor; its resistance decreases as light intensity increases.

flashcard_questions.q: What does NTC stand for in an NTC thermistor?
flashcard_questions.a: NTC stands for Negative Temperature Coefficient — resistance decreases as temperature rises.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the function of an analogue to digital converter (ADC)?
flashcard_questions.a: An ADC converts a continuously varying analogue signal into a binary digital number for processing.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the difference between a push-to-make and a push-to-break switch?
flashcard_questions.a: Push-to-make connects the circuit when pressed; push-to-break disconnects the circuit when pressed.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a Darlington driver and why is it used?
flashcard_questions.a: A Darlington driver pairs two NPN transistors to give very high current gain, used to drive high-power loads.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is a relay useful when connecting a microcontroller to a mains-powered device?
flashcard_questions.a: A relay provides electrical isolation, keeping the low-voltage control circuit separate from the mains-voltage load.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the difference between a polarised and a non-polarised capacitor?
flashcard_questions.a: A polarised capacitor has a positive and negative terminal and must be connected the correct way around.

flashcard_questions.q: What type of wiring is most suitable for connections that need to flex or move?
flashcard_questions.a: Multi-strand (flexible) wire is most suitable because it bends repeatedly without the conductor breaking.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one advantage of a photovoltaic cell as a power supply compared to a battery.
flashcard_questions.a: A photovoltaic cell is renewable and requires no replacement, making it more sustainable for long-term use.

flashcard_questions.q: What output device converts electrical energy into rotational mechanical movement?
flashcard_questions.a: A motor converts electrical energy into rotational mechanical movement.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the purpose of a reed switch and where is it typically used?
flashcard_questions.a: A reed switch closes when a magnet is nearby; it is typically used in door and window alarm sensors.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the difference between a lamp and an LED as output devices?
flashcard_questions.a: An LED is more efficient and longer-lasting than a lamp, and requires less current to produce light.
